title: Obex declares a direct-execution operating model, in tension with the layered governance its own Artifact specifies
content:
A.6.1.1.5.3.2.1 opens with an unusually direct claim about Obex's character: "Obex follows a **direct-execution model rather than a multi-layered governance system**." It names two key processes — **Incubation Selection**, where "projects are sourced, evaluated, and onboarded based on strategic fit, feasibility, and alignment with Sky objectives," and **Capital Allocation**, where "all allocations occur through the Obex Incubator Prime, which deploys first-loss or operational capital under predefined parameters."

Read against the rest of the Artifact, the statement is hard to reconcile. Amending the Artifact requires a 1% proposal threshold, an Operational Facilitator alignment finding, and a three-day token holder vote. The admin role over Obex's Liquidity Layer belongs to Sky Governance. Its executive function is delegated by Accord to a separate Executor Agent, Ozone. Its Liquidity Layer is operated by a development company contracted to a Foundation. That is a multi-layered governance system by any ordinary reading.

The reconciliation is probably scope: direct execution describes the **incubation business** — selecting and funding projects — not the Agent's constitutional machinery. "Under predefined parameters" is the load-bearing qualifier: speed comes from settling the parameters in advance so individual allocations need no fresh approval, which is the same pre-provisioning logic used throughout the Artifact.

Still, the sentence sits in the Artifact unqualified, and it is the kind of self-description that shapes expectations. A founder reading it expects fast decisions; a token holder reading the Root Edit section expects deliberation. Both are in the same document, and only the second is enforceable.
